chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who was performing Tamattu' (Hajj), he stood at Arafat and Al-Mash'ar, sacrificed his animal, and shaved his head. He said: 'He should not cover his head until he performs Tawaf with the House and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, for my father (peace be upon him) disliked that and forbade it.' We said: 'If he did it?' He said: 'I do not see anything upon him, but if he did not do it, it was more beloved to me.'
And when the Mu'tamatti' performs the Hajj visitation, everything is permissible for him except women, and we have clarified that, so there is no basis for repeating it.
And what he narrated: -(840) 33 - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Isma'il said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Is it permissible for the Muhrim al-Mutamatti' to touch perfume before performing Tawaf al-Nisa?' He said: 'No.'

So the ruling is what we mentioned previously, that it came as a recommendation (Istihbab) and leaving distraction by non-rituals, and that he should not use what is permissible for those who are released (from Ihram) except after completing all the rituals.

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَ الْمَرْوَةِ: As-Safa and Al-Marwah, the hills between which Sa'i is performed
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa, the final circumambulation of the Kaaba that concludes Hajj
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the main standing place during Hajj
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعاً: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in the same season

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a Mu'tamatti' pilgrim regarding shaving, covering the head, and using perfume during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that while covering the head before the final Tawaf is disliked based on his father's practice, it is not invalidating, whereas delaying the use of perfume until after all rituals are complete is a matter of recommended caution (istiḥbāb) to avoid distraction. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving the spiritual state of Ihram through the completion of all pillars, distinguishing between obligatory acts and recommended etiquettes. The prohibition of perfume specifically underscores the continuity of the ritual state until the full transition to the state of Ihlas (freedom from restrictions) is achieved.
